pol-nat-01-c2.text: John Breuilly (2016). Benedict Anderson's Imagined Communities: a symposium. Nations and Nationalism.
pol-nat-01-c2.quote: In an anthropological spirit, then, I propose the following definition of the nation: it is an imagined political community – and imagined as both inherently limited and sovereign.
pol-nat-01-c2.claim: Anderson defines the nation as 'an imagined political community, and imagined as both inherently limited and sovereign.'

pol-nat-01-c3.text: Ernest Gellner (1983). Excerpt from Nations and Nationalism. LSE Gellner archive (Cornell University Press, 1983).
pol-nat-01-c3.quote: The roots of nationalism in the distinctive structural requirements of industrial society are very deep indeed.
pol-nat-01-c3.claim: Ernest Gellner's Nations and Nationalism (1983) argued that nationalism is a functional consequence of industrial modernity.
